title: Erode, carry, drop: what waves do to a coast
examples: How do waves erode a cliff?

groups.label: Erode
groups.ask: How do waves erode a cliff?

explain.say: Stand on a beach and watch the waves. They are busy with three jobs all day long: breaking the land, carrying the bits away and dropping them somewhere new. Look at the board. We will sort the coast’s work into erode, carry and drop.

draw.text: Erode, carry, drop: what waves do to a coast

groups.label: Erode
groups.ask: How do waves erode a cliff?

explain.say: Look at the erode group. Erode means wear away. Hydraulic action is the force of water blasting air into cracks in a cliff. Abrasion is waves hurling pebbles at the cliff, like sandpaper. Attrition is pebbles bashing each other until they turn round. So why are beach pebbles smooth?

groups.label: Erode
groups.ask: How do waves erode a cliff?

explain.say: Now the carry group. Big stones roll along the sea bed, called traction, and sand grains bounce, called saltation. Waves also arrive at an angle and push sand along the beach in a zigzag. That is longshore drift. Can you picture sand marching along a beach?

groups.label: Erode
groups.ask: How do waves erode a cliff?

explain.say: See the drop group? When waves lose energy, in a calm bay or where the coast bends, they drop their load. That builds beaches, and spits, which are long fingers of sand, like Spurn Head in England. Where would you find the calmest water?

groups.label: Erode
groups.ask: How do waves erode a cliff?

explain.say: So a coast works like a factory line: erode, carry, drop, again and again. Wonderful work! Wow fact: the Curonian Spit, shared by Lithuania and Russia, is a ribbon of sand about 98 kilometres long, all built by waves.

groups.label: Erode
groups.ask: How do waves erode a cliff?

faq.q: How do waves erode a cliff?
faq.a: In four ways: hydraulic action, the force of water and squashed air in cracks; abrasion, pebbles thrown against the rock; attrition, pebbles knocking each other smaller; and solution, seawater slowly dissolving rocks like chalk and limestone.
Waves often reach the beach at an angle, pushing sand up the beach sideways. The water then runs straight back down the slope. Over and over, this zigzag carries sand along the coast.
asks: How does sand move along a beach?

faq.a: Waves drop sand where they lose energy: in sheltered bays, behind headlands and where the coast changes direction. This builds beaches, spits, sand bars and tombolos.
Attrition is when rocks carried by the waves knock against each other, chipping off their corners. Over time they become smaller, rounder pebbles and finally sand.
A tombolo is a bar of sand or pebbles that joins an island to the mainland. Chesil Beach in England links the Isle of Portland to the coast.
asks: Can a sand bar join an island to land?

facts: The Curonian Spit, shared by Lithuania and Russia, is about 98 km long and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Chesil Beach in England, about 29 km long, joins the Isle of Portland to the mainland.

quiz.say: Waves throw pebbles at a cliff and scrape it like sandpaper. What is this called?
quiz.show: Pebbles scraping a cliff like sandpaper is called…
quiz.why: Abrasion is the wearing away of rock by sand and pebbles thrown by the waves.

wrong.1: Longshore drift moves sand along the beach; it does not scrape cliffs.
wrong.2: Deposition means dropping sand, not wearing rock away.
